newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BELEAGURED BRIGHTON ANNOUNCE GROUND-SHARING PLAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BELEAGURED BRIGHTON ANNOUNCE GROUND-SHARING PLAN.

text.p: Brighton announced on Friday they had signed a deal to share Gillingham's ground for the next two seasons while a new ground is built in the Brighton area.

The south coast club, who face extinction just 13 years after playing Manchester United in the F.A. Cup final, announced in a statement issued by their chairman Bill Archer that he also welcomed the F.A.'s offer of independent arbitration in an attempt to break the deadlock over the club's future.
Archer said in a statement that, while he is prepared to take part in arbitration, he is making it clear that handing control to any one individual is not on the agenda.

The stay-away chairman, deeply unpopular with home fans and who no longer attends home matches, is appealing to supporters responsible for recent disturbances "to take their finger off the self-destruct button and get behind the team".
Archer concludes his statement by emphasising that the third division club are not going out of business and will have a new stadium for the 21st century.
Brighton's announcement that they are to groundshare with second division Gillingham follows rejections by both Portsmouth and Fulham to give them a temporary home.
The Football League have consistently stated that they cannot sanction any groundshare unless Brighton have firm plans in place for a new ground in the Brighton and Hove area.
This must include planning permission and so far Brighton's proposals for a new stadium at Toad's Hole Valley in Hove have met with failure from the local council.

The club, who played in the old first division for four years at the start of the 1980s are currently bottom of the third division and this week were dumped out of the first round of the F.A. Cup by non-league Sudbury Town.
